discovery: Discovery of Nd2Fe14B neodymium-iron-boron permanent magnets

nominees.name: Masato Sagawa
nominees.affiliation: NDFEB Corporation, Kyoto, Japan (formerly Sumitomo Special Metals)

nominees.name: John J. Croat
nominees.affiliation: John Croat Consulting, USA (formerly General Motors Research Laboratories)

subfield: Condensed matter physics / magnetism and magnetic materials
motivation: In 1982-84 Masato Sagawa (sintered route) and John Croat (rapid-quenched route) independently discovered permanent magnets based on the new tetragonal compound Nd2Fe14B. Against the prevailing belief that iron-rich rare-earth compounds could not give high coercivity and Curie temperature, they found a phase combining iron's large magnetisation with the strong uniaxial anisotropy of neodymium 4f electrons, achieving record energy products that remain unsurpassed after forty years. The discovery made avoidance of scarce cobalt possible and stimulated deep physics of crystal-field anisotropy, exchange coupling and coercivity mechanisms in nanostructured magnets. Its impact on society is immense: Nd-Fe-B magnets power electric vehicle motors, wind turbines, hard disks, MRI, robotics and nearly every compact electromechanical device, and are central to the energy transition. This is a model of materials discovery creating both new physics and transformative technology.
